title: Note on zero-sum magic squares on Abelian groups
summary: Let $(Γ,+)$ be an Abelian group of order $n^2$. A $Γ$-magic square of order $n$ is an $n\times n$ array whose entries are pairwise distinct elements of $Γ$ such that all row sums, column sums, and the two main diagonal sums are equal to the same element $μ\in Γ$, called the magic constant. A combinatorial design is called $Γ$-additive if its point set is a subset of an Abelian group $Γ$ and every block has sum zero.
